== Research Notes ==

A possible identification concerns Thomas Ross. The 1912 Belfast and Ulster Directory lists Thomas Ross as a mill owner at Gortreighy in the neighbourhood inhabitants section for Rasharkin. It adds a named economic and geographic associate in the townland where the Glasgow family lived in the earlier baptism period, but it does not establish any relationship to Alexander Glasgow or the McCaughan/Elder families.<ref>1912 Belfast and Ulster Directory, Rasharkin; [https://lennonwylie.co.uk/PT191214.htm record].</ref> Inspected named transcription or derivative source; original record uninspected and family identity not established. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Thomas Ross. The original 1901 Gortereghy return describes Thomas Ross, 34, as farmer and flax miller, with Scotland-born wife Mary Jane and six children. This supplies an occupation bridge to the 1912 mill-owner directory entry; the 1911 return records 24 years of marriage and seven surviving children. [[Ross-13124]] remains compatible; the reported census ages differ.<ref>1901 Gortereghy, Thomas Ross household; [https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai000298459.pdf record]; 1911 Gortereghy, Thomas Ross household; [https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390150.pdf record].</ref> The identification remains uncertain.
